To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the optimal sensor scheduling for remote state estimation is a difference of convex function, and (ii) locally optimal sensor scheduling decisions can be computed by solving a sequence of convex programs.
data-driven sensor scheduling can be formulated as difference of convex programs, and locally optimal schedules can be found by applying the convex-concave procedure.

the optimal data-driven sensor scheduling for remote state estimation in a unicast network can be obtained by solving a difference of convex program and the optimal data-driven scheduling for a broadcast network can be obtained via solving a difference of concave-convex program, where the convex and concave parts are given in closed-form.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of a new data driven sensor scheduling approach that is applicable to a broad class of problems in wireless sensor networks.

the following questions: How to schedule the sensors in a network to minimize the error in estimating a remote state, if no prior knowledge of the data's distribution is assumed? How does this approach compare to other methods? What are the advantages of our approach? How can it be extended to other problems?

the following questions: (i) Can sensor scheduling be performed without a probabilistic model of sensor observations? (ii) Can sensor scheduling decisions be made based on data? (iii) Can the data driven sensor scheduling be done efficiently?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is a viable and promising alternative to the traditional probabilistic model-based sensor scheduling approaches.
the proposed framework for sensor scheduling based on data-driven empirical risk minimization is a viable approach for remote estimation problems in wireless networks.

data-driven scheduling is an attractive and promising approach to sensor scheduling, which is particularly suitable for wireless sensor networks where the underlying probabilistic models are not known or are too difficult to model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a data-driven approach for sensor scheduling for both unicast and broadcast networks.
the sensor scheduling problem can be formulated as an empirical risk minimization problem, where the empirical risk minimizer is obtained efficiently by the convex concave algorithm.
we have proposed a data driven approach for sensor scheduling in wireless networks, which is based solely on the data, without any assumptions on the underlying probabilistic models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the data driven sensor scheduling framework is applicable to a broad class of remote estimation problems, and it is computationally tractable.
sensor scheduling can be performed efficiently without knowledge of the underlying model, but rather based on observed data only.
, in contrast with the existing literature, the proposed approach is applicable even when the underlying probabilistic models are not known.
